title: The EYERISING Study
official: Repeated Low-level Red Light for Myopia Progression Study: An International, Multicenter, Multiethnic, Randomized Controlled Trial, IPOSC Study
summary:
The purpose of this clinical trial is to see if and how well Repeated Low-Level Red Light (RLRL) therapy works to control myopia over 12 months. The main question it aims to answer is:

* Can RLRL therapy help slow down the worsening of myopia?

Participants will use a red-light therapy investigational device at home, 5 days a week for 12 months.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age ≥ 6 and ≤ 12 (at screening)
* Myopia: Cycloplegic SER -1.0 to -7.0 D
* Astigmatism: \< 1.5 D
* Anisometropia: \< 1.5 D
* Informed parental consent
* Consistent access to wireless internet

Exclusion Criteria:

* A subject who is born female and who is currently menstruating or has begun menstruation (menarche).

  * Ophthalmic diseases, conditions, or syndromes other than refractive errors
  * Previous use of treatment for myopia control (e.g., defocusing lenses or contact lenses, orthokeratology, atropine, and pirenzepine)
  * Any previous ocular surgery
  * Systemic diseases (e.g., endocrine, cardiac diseases) and developmental anomalies
  * Inability to attend regular follow up visits
  * Participants with any symptom, disease, or other condition that, in the opinion of the investigators, may affect the effectiveness of the investigational treatment and/or the ability of the participant to complete study activities
